full_judgment:
D.C. Bhattacharya, J.—This Rule is directed against an order passed by the last Court 4 Subordinate Judge, Dacca in Title Execution Case No. 22 of 1968 purporting to stay the execution case till the disposal of the First Appeal preferred by the judgment-debtor against the decree under execution. 

 2. The petitioner’s case is that the petitioner brought a suit against the Government of Pakistan for a declaration of his title to certain properties and for recovery of possession of the said properties as well as for mesne profits. The suit was decreed in part with cost allowing the prayers of the plaintiff in respect of a part of the suit properties. The decretal cost was assessed at a sum of Taka 2,965/-. The petitioner thereafter put the decree for post into execution on 1-4-68, whereupon the above mentioned Execution Case was started, 

 3. It appears that the Government of Pakistan preferred an appeal against the said decree in the Dacca High Court being First Appeal No. 8 of 1967 which was pending at the time of the filing of the aforesaid execution case. 

 "Decree-holder files hazira. No stay order obtained and filed by the judgment-debtor. 

 5. Mr. Akram Hossain Amin, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the decree-holder petitioner submits that the learned Subordinate Judge as the executing court acted beyond jurisdiction in staying the further proceeding of the execution case merely on the ground that an appeal was pending against the decree which was under execution. Mr. Kari Shafiuddin who filed power on behalf of the Government of Pakistan submits that he has no instruction in the matter from the Government of Bangladesh which is deemed to have been substituted in place of the Government of Pakistan under the provision of President's Order No. 69 of 1972. Mr. Ismailuddin Sarker, the learned Assistant Attorney-General also submits that he has no instruction in the matter. 

 6. An executing court can stay the exertion of an appealable decree before expiration of the time allowed for appeal there from under sub-rule (2) of rule 5 of Order 41 of the Code of Civil Procedure and when an appeal has been filed, the executing court can stay the execution under sub-rule (2) of rule 6 when an order has been made for sale of immovable properties pending the hearing of the appeal on such terms as to giving security or otherwise as the court thinks fit. In the instant case an appeal having been filed already in the High Court time was granted twice for obtaining stay order from the High. Court but when no such stay order could be brought by the judgment-debtor the executing court itself stayed the further proceeding of the Execution case till the disposal of the appeal. This is clearly beyond the jurisdiction of the executing court. After the filing of the appeal it is generally the appellate court which can stay the execution of the decree tinder Order 41 rule 5 of the Code and it is only under the conditions mentioned in Order 41 rule 6(2) of the Code that the executing court itself can stay the execution of the decree. As there is no order for the sale of the property in the execution case the executing court was not within its power to stay the execution case and it did not even make any order as to the security to be furnished as is contemplated in the said provision of the Code. We are, therefore, of the opinion that the executing court acted without jurisdiction in passing the impugned order.
